summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing a seizure during hemodialysis, which was likely due to missing his morning doses of Keppra and Trileptal. He has a history of seizure disorder closely tied to medication noncompliance around dialysis sessions. Initial concern for pneumonia based on a preliminary chest X-ray was ruled out after a final read showed only atelectasis and no clinical or lab evidence of infection. He underwent a full hemodialysis session the following day without complications. His vancomycin course for a prior possible line infection was continued as planned, with a therapeutic level confirmed. Medication access was an issue as he lost his prescriptions and could not refill them before discharge; he was sent home with a 24-hour supply and instructions to refill on Monday. He was discharged home in stable condition with reinforced education on medication timing and adherence.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
